record.original_question: Let a1 = a, a2, … be a geometric progression with positive first term a and positive ratio r ≠ 1. Let n and k be natural numbers with n > k + 1. If A is the sum of the first k terms and B is the sum of the last k terms among the first n terms, express the ratio r solely in terms of A and B, and also express the first term a solely in terms of A and B.

evidence.quote: Suppose that n and k are natural numbers such that n > k + 1; and a1 = a, a2, . . . , at, . . . a geometric progression, with positive ratio r 6= 1, and positive first term a. If A is the value of the sum of the first k terms of the progression and B is the value of the last k terms among the n first terms, express the ratio r in terms of A and B only; and also the first term a in terms of A and B.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be a geometric progression of real numbers with positive first term $a_1 = a > 0$ and positive common ratio $r > 0$ with $r 
eq 1$, so that $a_i = a\, r^{\,i-1}$ for every positive integer $i$. Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers satisfying $n > k+1$. Define
$$A = a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_k, \qquad B = a_{n-k+1} + a_{n-k+2} + \cdots + a_n,$$
i.e. $A$ is the sum of the first $k$ terms and $B$ is the sum of the last $k$ terms among the first $n$ terms of the progression.

Express the common ratio $r$ as an explicit formula in $A$ and $B$ (with $n$ and $k$ as given parameters), and likewise express the first term $a$ as an explicit formula in $A$ and $B$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a standard exercise on geometric progressions with an elementary closed-form solution: since the last $k$ terms equal $r^{n-k}$ times the first $k$ terms, one has $B = A\, r^{n-k}$, hence $r = (B/A)^{1/(n-k)}$ and $a = A(r-1)/(r^k-1)$. No active research status.
